label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
@Kavya [surname], I'm tagging you because I'd rather say this openly than keep it in comments. Some of your post is true and some isn't, so here's my side.

For anyone who missed the context: Kavya and I are both from Foundry91 Cohort 4 (demo day March 2026). Her company is SitterNest, babysitter booking. Mine is DabbaDost, home tiffin subscriptions. We hire from the same small pool of engineers in HSR and Koramangala.

Let me start with the part that's on me. Two people from Kavya's team joined us this month, and that's correct. What I didn't do was tell her. I knew where they worked from day one, and I should have called her before making any offers. I didn't, and that's my mistake.

Here's what actually happened. On 14 September we posted a backend developer opening on our LinkedIn page and on Instahyre, open to anyone. The first candidate applied on his own on 19 September. The second came about two weeks later as a referral from him. Nobody on my side DMed anyone at SitterNest.

The offer was 22% over their current CTC, not 40%. Both joined on 3 November. If you've been repeating 40 in the comments, please change it to 22.

On ESOPs, Kavya wrote that we promised options we don't even have. That's not accurate. We have an ESOP pool. It's small, but it's real, documented, and on paper since January.

I also want to be clear about something. Kavya sat with me until 1am in our Koramangala office, fixing our Razorpay webhook mess before demo day. I haven't forgotten that, and it's part of why this has been hard to watch. After the second offer was accepted, I sent her a WhatsApp. It got a blue tick and no reply. Then the post went up. A conversation at that point would have prevented a lot of this.

I'm not writing this to fight. I don't want a public fight with someone who has helped me this much. I'm writing it because in a batch of 11 startups, this will keep happening unless we agree on how to handle it.

So here's a simple rule for our cohort: if you're interviewing someone from another batch company, give that founder a heads up before you make an offer. One message. It would have saved all of us this week.

Kavya, the coffee or call is open. This week, whenever you're comfortable. No agenda and no PR. I'd like to talk to you as the person who sat with me at 1am.

To everyone else in the batch, sorry this ended up in your feeds. Let's keep the next one a conversation, not a comment thread.

---

Notes: It's about 430 words and roughly 2,500 characters, so it fits both limits. Replace "@Kavya [surname]" with her actual LinkedIn tag before posting. The two engineers aren't named anywhere.
